symbols.name: r
symbols.def: The declared polynomial degree of the untreated calendar trend.

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: The largest lag whose treatment indicator enters the fixed potential outcome.

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: Measured stages are indexed by \(t=1,\ldots,T\); the pre-rollout endpoint \(t=0\) fixes treatment fraction zero but is not an outcome measurement.

symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of fixed units repeatedly observed throughout the rollout.

symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: The target upper bound on asymptotic noncoverage in the open inference question.

symbols.name: z_alpha
symbols.def: \(z_\alpha=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\).

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: \(p=(p_0,\ldots,p_T)\) is the precommitted threshold schedule.

symbols.name: p_ext
symbols.def: \(p^{\mathrm{ext}}_s=0\) for \(s\le 0\), \(p^{\mathrm{ext}}_s=p_s\) for \(s\in J_T\), and \(p^{\mathrm{ext}}_s=1\) for \(s>T\).

symbols.name: U
symbols.def: \(U=(U_i)_{i\in I_n}\) is the sole source of design randomness.

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: \(Z_{i,t}=\mathbf 1\{U_i\le p^{\mathrm{ext}}_t\}\).

symbols.name: Z_paths
symbols.def: \(\mathcal Z(p)\) is the set of treatment histories generated by the assignment construction \(Z\) as one unit score ranges over \([0,1]\), using the endpoint convention \(p^{\mathrm{ext}}\).

symbols.name: g
symbols.def: \(g_{i,t}\) is unit \(i\)'s fixed untreated secular component at measured stage \(t\).

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: \(a_{i,j}\) is unit \(i\)'s coefficient on \(t^j\) in the secular component.

symbols.name: b
symbols.def: \(b_{i,\ell}\) is unit \(i\)'s causal coefficient on treatment at lag \(\ell\).

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: \(Y_{i,t}(z)\) is fixed before \(U\) is drawn.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: \(B_i=\max_{t\in J_T,\ z\in\mathcal Z(p)}|Y_{i,t}(z)|\) for \(i\in I_n\).

symbols.name: Y_obs
symbols.def: \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{i,t}=Y_{i,t}(Z_{i,\cdot})\) for \(i\in I_n\) and \(t\in J_T\); the full repeatedly observed unit-level panel is available to a feasible inference rule.

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: \(M_t=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_n}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{i,t}\) for \(t\in J_T\).

symbols.name: bar_a
symbols.def: \(\bar a_j=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_n}a_{i,j}\) for \(j=0,\ldots,r\).

symbols.name: beta
symbols.def: \(\beta_\ell=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_n}b_{i,\ell}\) for \(\ell=0,\ldots,L\).

symbols.name: eta
symbols.def: \(\eta=(\bar a_0,\ldots,\bar a_r,\beta_0,\ldots,\beta_L)^{\mathsf T}\).

symbols.name: theta
symbols.def: \(\theta=\sum_{\ell=0}^{L}\beta_\ell=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_n}\sum_{\ell=0}^{L}b_{i,\ell}\).

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: Row \(t\in J_T\) is \(X_t=(1,t,\ldots,t^r,p^{\mathrm{ext}}_t,p^{\mathrm{ext}}_{t-1},\ldots,p^{\mathrm{ext}}_{t-L})\).

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: \(c=(0,\ldots,0,1,\ldots,1)^{\mathsf T}\), with \(r+1\) zeros and \(L+1\) ones, so \(c^{\mathsf T}\eta=\theta\).

symbols.name: w
symbols.def: \(w=(w_1,\ldots,w_T)^{\mathsf T}\) forms the linear estimator \(w^{\mathsf T}M\).

symbols.name: W_c
symbols.def: \(\mathcal W_c(p)=\{w\in\mathbb R^T:X^{\mathsf T}w=c\}\).

symbols.name: T_min
symbols.def: \(T_{\min}(r,L)=\min\{T:\exists p\text{ with }0=p_0\le\cdots\le p_T=1\text{ and }\mathcal W_c(p)\ne\varnothing\}\).

symbols.name: p_star
symbols.def: For \(t=0,\ldots,T\), \(p_t^\star=\binom{t+r}{r+1}/\binom{T+r}{r+1}\).

symbols.name: w_star
symbols.def: \(w_t^\star=\binom{T+r}{r+1}(-1)^{T-t}\binom{r+1}{T-t}\mathbf 1\{0\le T-t\le r+1\}\) for \(t\in J_T\).

symbols.name: q_p
symbols.def: \(q_p(x)=-\sum_{s=1}^{T}p_s\prod_{u\in J_T,\ u\ne s}(x-u)/(s-u)\), whose degree is at most \(T-1\).

symbols.name: Gamma
symbols.def: \(\Gamma(p,b)=\operatorname{Cov}_U(M)\), with covariance taken only over the known hash randomization.

symbols.name: w_Gamma
symbols.def: \(w_\Gamma\) is the minimum-Euclidean-norm element of \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in\mathcal W_c(p)}v^{\mathsf T}\Gamma v\).

symbols.name: hat_theta_Gamma
symbols.def: \(\widehat\theta_\Gamma=w_\Gamma^{\mathsf T}M\).

symbols.name: R_Gamma
symbols.def: \(R_\Gamma=w_\Gamma^{\mathsf T}\Gamma w_\Gamma=\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\theta_\Gamma)\).

symbols.name: hat_Gamma
symbols.def: \(\widehat\Gamma\) is a positive-semidefinite, observed-data-measurable estimate produced by the admissible unit-level learning rule in Definition \(\mathrm{def:hajek\text{-}inference\text{-}handle}\).

symbols.name: hat_w
symbols.def: \(\widehat w\) is the exact-balance weight output of the admissible covariance-and-weight learning rule, with \(X^{\mathsf T}\widehat w=c\) almost surely.

symbols.name: hat_theta
symbols.def: \(\widehat\theta\) is the symmetrized unit-cross-fitted estimator output by the inference construction handle.

symbols.name: hat_V
symbols.def: \(\widehat V\) is the observable unit-clustered sandwich variance output by the inference construction handle.

symbols.name: H_Hajek
symbols.def: The handle starts from a unit-entry-time H\'{a}jek projection, learns a positive-semidefinite covariance and exact-balance weights by unit-level cross-fitting or leave-one-unit-out symmetrization, retains every within-unit cross-stage product generated by the shared score \(U_i\), and permits only regularization that vanishes as \(n\to\infty\).

symbols.name: E_panel
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{panel}}(p)\) is the class of observed-panel statistics that are exactly design-unbiased for \(\theta\) uniformly over the fixed additive-lag arrays.

symbols.name: T_min_panel
symbols.def: \(T_{\min}^{\mathrm{panel}}(L)\) is the least measured-stage count admitting an exactly design-unbiased observed-panel estimator of \(\theta\).

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: \(A_i=\mathbf 1\{U_i\le p_1\}\).

symbols.name: hat_theta_panel
symbols.def: \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{panel}}\) is the endpoint Horvitz--Thompson estimator defined from stages \(1\) and \(T\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: \(H\) is the number of rollout periods, including the terminal period at which the treatment fraction equals one.

symbols.name: S
symbols.def: \(\mathcal S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,H\}\) is the set of rollout stages at which outcomes are observed.

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: \(m=|\mathcal S|\) is the outcome-measurement cost.

symbols.name: E_wave
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{wave}}(p,\mathcal S)\) is the class of observed-wave statistics that are exactly design-unbiased for \(\theta\) uniformly over the fixed additive-lag arrays.

symbols.name: F_wave
symbols.def: \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{wave}}(L)\) is the set of feasible horizon and outcome-wave-count pairs for exact design-unbiased estimation of \(\theta\).

symbols.name: m_min_wave
symbols.type: minimum outcome-wave count at a fixed horizon
symbols.def: \(m_{\min}^{\mathrm{wave}}(H,L)\) is the lower envelope of \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{wave}}(L)\) at horizon \(H\).

symbols.name: hat_theta_one
symbols.def: \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{one}}(t)\) is the one-wave Horvitz--Thompson contrast between units exposed throughout all relevant lags and units exposed at none of them.

symbols.name: G_wave
symbols.def: For a selected measured wave \(s\), \(G_{i,s}=\mathbf 1\{p_{s-1}<U_i\leq p_s\}\) indicates adoption at that wave.

symbols.name: N_wave
symbols.def: For a selected measured wave \(s\), \(N_{i,s}=\mathbf 1\{U_i>p_s\}\) indicates no treatment through that wave.

symbols.name: hat_theta_elbow
symbols.def: \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{elbow}}(s)\) combines the new-adopter versus never-yet-treated contrast at nonterminal wave \(s\) with the early-adopter versus terminal-adopter contrast at wave \(H=L+1\).

symbols.name: Q_wave
symbols.def: \(\mathcal Q_t(p)=\{q\in(0,1):q=p^{\mathrm{ext}}_{t-\ell}\text{ for some }\ell\in\{0,\ldots,L\}\}\) is the set of distinct interior thresholds at observed wave \(t\).

symbols.name: v_wave
symbols.def: For \(t\in\mathcal S\) and \(q\in\mathcal Q_t(p)\), \((v_{t,q})_\ell=\mathbf 1\{p^{\mathrm{ext}}_{t-\ell}=q\}\) for \(\ell=0,\ldots,L\).

symbols.name: V_wave
symbols.def: \(\mathcal V(p,\mathcal S)=\operatorname{span}\{v_{t,q}:t\in\mathcal S,\ q\in\mathcal Q_t(p)\}\subseteq\mathbb R^{L+1}\).

assumptions.condition: The potential-outcome panel \(Y\), the secular components \(g\), and the lag coefficients \(b\) are fixed before \(U\) is drawn.
The coordinates \(U_i\), \(i\in I_n\), are independent \(\operatorname{Uniform}[0,1]\) scores.
For every \(i\in I_n\), \(t\in J_T\), and own-treatment history \(z\in\{0,1\}^{\mathbb Z}\), \(Y_{i,t}(z)=g_{i,t}+\sum_{\ell=0}^{L}b_{i,\ell}z_{t-\ell}\).

novel.justification: This maintained restriction allows each unit to have its own finite impulse-response profile while ruling out treatment-history interactions beyond the declared lag horizon. It has direct empirical meaning in short product or policy ramps where exposure at each recent stage contributes additively but response magnitudes differ across units.

This maintained restriction permits every unit to have a distinct level, slope, and higher-order secular profile while requiring those profiles to lie in one prespecified low-degree calendar basis. It is empirically interpretable for short rollout windows in which unit-specific baseline trajectories are smooth enough to be represented by a declared polynomial degree.

assumptions.condition: Along the triangular array indexed by \(n\to\infty\) with \(T\), \(r\), and \(L\) fixed, there exists a constant \(C_4<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that \(n^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_n}B_i^4\le C_4\) for every \(n\).

standard.name: Uniform fourth-moment sufficient condition for finite-population Lindeberg regularity

assumptions.condition: Along the triangular array indexed by \(n\to\infty\) with \(T\), \(r\), and \(L\) fixed, \(\sum_{j\in I_n}B_j^2>0\) for all sufficiently large \(n\) and \(\max_{i\in I_n}B_i^2/\sum_{j\in I_n}B_j^2\to0\).
Along the triangular array indexed by \(n\to\infty\) with \(T\), \(r\), and \(L\) fixed, the oracle risk satisfies \(0<\liminf_{n\to\infty}nR_\Gamma\le\limsup_{n\to\infty}nR_\Gamma<\infty\).

standard.name: Positive finite limiting variance under root-\(n\) normalization

definitions.name: Binomial-ramp and terminal-difference construction
definitions.construction: Set \(T=\max\{r+2,L+1\}\), \(p_t^\star=\binom{t+r}{r+1}/\binom{T+r}{r+1}\) for \(t=0,\ldots,T\), and \(w_t^\star=\binom{T+r}{r+1}(-1)^{T-t}\binom{r+1}{T-t}\mathbf 1\{0\le T-t\le r+1\}\) for \(t\in J_T\).

definitions.name: Explicit support-deficit alias
definitions.construction: If \(T\le L\), use the coefficient direction with unit loading on \(\beta_L\) and zero elsewhere. If \(T\le r+1\), use unit loading on \(\beta_0\) and polynomial nuisance perturbation \(q_p(x)=-\sum_{s=1}^{T}p_s\prod_{u\in J_T,\ u\ne s}(x-u)/(s-u)\).

definitions.name: Singular-covariance oracle representer
definitions.construction: \(w_\Gamma\) is the minimum-Euclidean-norm minimizer of \(v^{\mathsf T}\Gamma v\) subject to \(X^{\mathsf T}v=c\), and \(\widehat\theta_\Gamma=w_\Gamma^{\mathsf T}M\).

definitions.name: Observed-panel cross-fitted H\'{a}jek inference handle
definitions.construction: With \(T\), \(r\), and \(L\) fixed as \(n\to\infty\), restrict attention to permutation-invariant rules measurable with respect to the observed unit-level panel \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}\), the realized scores \(U\), and the known schedule \(p\). Start from the unit-entry-time H\'{a}jek projection, estimate a positive-semidefinite covariance by unit-level cross-fitting or leave-one-unit-out symmetrization, solve the exact-balance constraint \(X^{\mathsf T}\widehat w=c\) within each training fold, and retain all within-unit cross-stage products in \(\widehat V\). No rule may use the unobserved coefficients \(a\) or \(b\); any eigenvalue regularization must vanish as \(n\to\infty\).

definitions.name: Panel endpoint-overlap condition
definitions.construction:
For \(T\ge2\), a schedule has panel endpoint overlap when
\[
 0=p_0<p_1\le p_2\le\cdots\le p_{T-1}<p_T=1.
\]
Thus the early-adopter probability \(p_1\), the stage-one control probability \(1-p_1\), and the terminal-adopter probability \(1-p_{T-1}\) are all strictly positive; equality at intermediate rollout stages is allowed.

definitions.name: Exactly unbiased observed-panel rules
definitions.construction: For fixed \(n,L,T\) and endpoint schedule \(p\), let \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{panel}}(p)\) be the set of integrable real-valued statistics measurable with respect to \(\sigma(Y^{\mathrm{obs}},U,Z,p)\) whose design expectation equals \(\theta\) for every fixed pair of arrays \((g,b)\) and potential-outcome panel satisfying Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:fixed\text{-}potential\text{-}outcomes}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:additive\text{-}distributed\text{-}lag}\).  The secular array \(g\) is unrestricted across units and measured stages in this class.

definitions.name: Observed-panel stage frontier
definitions.construction:
Define the observed-panel stage frontier by
\[
 T_{\min}^{\mathrm{panel}}(L)
 =\min\left\{T\in\mathbb N:\ 
 \begin{array}{l}
 \text{there exists }p\text{ with }0=p_0\le\cdots\le p_T=1\\
 \text{and }\mathcal E_{\mathrm{panel}}(p)\ne\varnothing
 \end{array}
 \right\}.
\]

definitions.name: Endpoint Horvitz--Thompson panel estimator
Exactly unbiased outcome-wave rules
definitions.construction:
For a rollout horizon \(H\in\mathbb N\), instantiate the assignment and potential-outcome model at \(T=H\).  Let \(\mathcal S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,H\}\) be the set of stages at which outcomes are revealed.  Define \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{wave}}(p,\mathcal S)\) to be the set of integrable real-valued statistics measurable with respect to
\[
 \sigma\!\left(U,Z,p,
       (Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{i,t})_{i\in I_n,\ t\in\mathcal S}\right)
\]
whose design expectation equals \(\theta\) for every fixed pair \((g,b)\) satisfying Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:fixed\text{-}potential\text{-}outcomes}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:additive\text{-}distributed\text{-}lag}\).  The secular values \(g_{i,t}\) are unrestricted across units and stages.  The scores and assignments may be observed at all rollout stages, but outcomes outside \(\mathcal S\) are not available to a statistic in this class.

definitions.name: Bivariate rollout-horizon/outcome-wave frontier
definitions.construction:
For \(L\in\mathbb N_0\), define
\[
 \mathcal F_{\mathrm{wave}}(L)
 =\left\{(H,m)\in\mathbb N^2:
 \begin{array}{l}
 \text{there exist }p\text{ with }0=p_0\leq\cdots\leq p_H=1
 \text{ and }\mathcal S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,H\},\\
 |\mathcal S|=m\text{ and }\mathcal E_{\mathrm{wave}}(p,\mathcal S)\ne\varnothing
 \end{array}
 \right\}.
\]
Set
\[
 m_{\min}^{\mathrm{wave}}(H,L)
 =\min\{m\in\mathbb N:(H,m)\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{wave}}(L)\},
\]
with the value \(+\infty\) when the displayed set is empty.

definitions.name: Interior one-wave Horvitz--Thompson estimator
definitions.construction:
Fix a horizon \(H\), a measured occasion \(t\in\{1,\ldots,H\}\), and an irreversible endpoint schedule.  If
\[
 0<p^{\mathrm{ext}}_{t-L}\leq p_t<1,
\]
define the full-history and no-history indicators
\[
 D_{i,t}=\mathbf 1\{U_i\leq p^{\mathrm{ext}}_{t-L}\},
 \qquad
 N_{i,t}=\mathbf 1\{U_i>p_t\},
\]
and the interior one-wave Horvitz--Thompson estimator
\[
 \widehat\theta_{\mathrm{one}}(t)
 =\frac1n\sum_{i\in I_n}
 \left\{
 \frac{D_{i,t}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{i,t}}{p^{\mathrm{ext}}_{t-L}}
 -\frac{N_{i,t}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{i,t}}{1-p_t}
 \right\}.
\]
Both denominators are strictly positive under the displayed condition.

definitions.name: Placement-specific elbow Horvitz--Thompson estimator
definitions.construction:
Fix \(L\geq1\), instantiate \(T=H=L+1\), choose \(s\in\{1,\ldots,L\}\), and suppose that the irreversible endpoint schedule also satisfies
\[
 0<p_1,\qquad p_{s-1}<p_s,\qquad p_L<1.
\]
Define the new-adopter and never-yet-treated indicators at wave \(s\) by
\[
 G_{i,s}=\mathbf 1\{p_{s-1}<U_i\leq p_s\},
 \qquad
 N_{i,s}=\mathbf 1\{U_i>p_s\},
 \qquad i\in I_n.
\]
With \(A_i=\mathbf 1\{U_i\leq p_1\}\) and \(C_i=\mathbf 1\{U_i>p_L\}\), define
\[
 \widehat\theta_{\mathrm{elbow}}(s)
 =\frac1n\sum_{i\in I_n}
 \left\{
 \frac{G_{i,s}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{i,s}}{p_s-p_{s-1}}
 -\frac{N_{i,s}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{i,s}}{1-p_s}
 +\frac{A_iY^{\mathrm{obs}}_{i,H}}{p_1}
 -\frac{C_iY^{\mathrm{obs}}_{i,H}}{1-p_L}
 \right\}.
\]
The four denominators are strictly positive: the first, third, and fourth by the displayed conditions, and the second because monotonicity and \(s\leq L\) give \(p_s\leq p_L<1\).  The statistic uses outcomes only at waves \(s\) and \(H\).

definitions.name: Observed-wave threshold-block span
definitions.construction:
Fix a rollout horizon \(H\), instantiate \(T=H\), fix an irreversible endpoint schedule \(p\), and let \(\mathcal S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,H\}\).  For each \(t\in\mathcal S\), define the finite set of distinct interior thresholds
\[
 \mathcal Q_t(p)
 =\left\{q\in(0,1):q=p^{\mathrm{ext}}_{t-\ell}
       \text{ for some }\ell\in\{0,\ldots,L\}\right\}.
\]
For \(q\in\mathcal Q_t(p)\), define the threshold-block vector \(v_{t,q}\in\mathbb R^{L+1}\) componentwise by
\[
 (v_{t,q})_\ell
 =\mathbf 1\{p^{\mathrm{ext}}_{t-\ell}=q\},
 \qquad \ell=0,\ldots,L.
\]
The fixed-schedule observed-wave block space is
\[
 \mathcal V(p,\mathcal S)
 =\operatorname{span}\left\{v_{t,q}:
       t\in\mathcal S,\ q\in\mathcal Q_t(p)\right\}
 \subseteq\mathbb R^{L+1},
\]
where the span of the empty family is \(\{0\}\).

statements.statement:
Under Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:fixed	ext{-}potential	ext{-}outcomes}\), \(\mathrm{ass:nested	ext{-}hash	ext{-}randomization}\), \(\mathrm{ass:additive	ext{-}distributed	ext{-}lag}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:polynomial	ext{-}secular	ext{-}trend}\), with assignment \(Z\) defined by the common-score threshold construction, \(\mathbb E_U[M]=X\eta\). The finite-population contrast \(	heta=c^{\mathsf T}\eta\) is identified by a linear functional of the stage means if and only if \(c\in\operatorname{row}(X)\), equivalently \(\mathcal W_c(p)
e\varnothing\). Every \(w\in\mathcal W_c(p)\) gives \(\mathbb E_U[w^{\mathsf T}M]=	heta\). If \(c
otin\operatorname{row}(X)\), there exists \(h\in\ker(X)\) with \(c^{\mathsf T}h
e0\), so \(\eta\) and \(\eta+h\) have the same mean path and different sustained contrasts.
statements.justification: This separates target estimability from full identification of all trend and lag coefficients.
statements.gap: This is the classical linear-model \(c\)-estimability certificate, not the novel contribution. Elfving1952, KieferWolfowitz1959, and Studden1968 provide the adjacent scalar-optimal-design geometry; the new content begins with the constrained monotone polynomial-lag support frontier below.
statements.consumer: A rollout operator can audit a proposed fraction path before using any cumulative-effect estimator.

statements.statement: Under Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:irreversible\text{-}endpoints}\), \(\mathrm{ass:additive\text{-}distributed\text{-}lag}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:polynomial\text{-}secular\text{-}trend}\), the sharp minimum measured-stage count is \(T_{\min}(r,L)=\max\{r+2,L+1\}\). At \(T=\max\{r+2,L+1\}\), the construction in Definition \(\mathrm{def:canonical\text{-}frontier\text{-}design}\) satisfies \(0=p_0^\star<p_1^\star<\cdots<p_T^\star=1\) and \(X(p^\star)^{\mathsf T}w^\star=c\). For every deficit \(T<\max\{r+2,L+1\}\), Definition \(\mathrm{def:deficit\text{-}alias}\) gives a target-active null direction: the lag-\(L\) column is zero when \(T\le L\), while the direct-treatment column is absorbed by a degree-at-most-\(T-1\) nuisance polynomial when \(T\le r+1\).
statements.justification: The formula is an optimal-design certificate: the binomial ramp attains the smallest operational stage budget and the two explicit alias families certify necessity.
statements.gap: Classical \(c\)-estimability and \(c\)-optimal polynomial-regression theory optimize a scalar contrast over generic design measures or Chebyshev systems, but do not impose one endpoint-attaining monotone path whose shifted copies form all carryover columns. AboukhamseenHudaBose2021 obtains universally optimal two-period non-circular multi-treatment crossover sequence designs for direct-plus-carryover contrasts under correlated errors, not a stage-support frontier for one irreversible threshold path with degree-\(r\) calendar nuisance and arbitrary lag order. XiongAtheyBayatiImbens2023 gives \(T\)-period GLS-based trace-precision optimality conditions under a specified lag model, and CortezEichhornYu2022 counts interpolation nodes for one polynomial response; none gives the exact formula \(\max\{r+2,L+1\}\), its monotone attainability, or both target-active deficit aliases.
statements.consumer: A deterministic-hash platform can decide whether a planned multi-stage ramp contains enough calendar support to estimate the sustained effect before committing traffic.

statements.statement: For \(r=L=1\), three measured stages suffice: \(p=(p_0,p_1,p_2,p_3)=(0,1/6,1/2,1)\) and \(w=(6,-12,6)^{\mathsf T}\) satisfy \(X^{\mathsf T}w=(0,0,1,1)^{\mathsf T}\). The supplied four-stage check is also correct: for \(p=(0,0,0,1/2,1)\), the measured \(4\times4\) matrix has determinant \(1/4\), and \(w=(2,-2,-2,2)^{\mathsf T}\) satisfies the same identity. In contrast, for every \(T\ge3\), the linear ramp \(p_t=t/T\) is nonidentifying because the coefficient perturbation with direct-effect loading \(1\), time-trend loading \(-1/T\), and all other loadings zero lies in \(\ker(X)\) and changes \(\theta\) by \(1\).
statements.justification: These exact reductions pass the early-kill test and show why nonconstant rollout variation alone is insufficient.
statements.gap: The four-stage identity was presolve evidence, but the three-stage witness and the target-active linear-ramp alias sharpen it and prevent an incorrect four-stage minimum claim.
statements.consumer: The proposition is a unit test for schedule-audit software and a warning against default linear ramps under linear calendar drift.

statements.statement: Fix \(T\), \(r\), and \(L\), and let \(n\to\infty\) through finite populations satisfying the maintained structural and randomization assumptions together with Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}population\text{-}fourth\text{-}moment\), \(\mathrm{ass:max\text{-}unit\text{-}lindeberg\), and \(\mathrm{ass:nondegenerate\text{-}oracle\text{-}risk\). The observed data are the full unit-level panel \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}\), the realized scores \(U\), the assignment panel \(Z\), and the known schedule \(p\). Using only the admissible covariance-and-weight learning rules in Definition \(\mathrm{def:hajek\text{-}inference\text{-}handle\), can one construct \(\widehat\Gamma\), exact-balance weights \(\widehat w\), an estimator \(\widehat\theta\), and \(\widehat V\) such that uniformly over this class, \(\mathbb E_U[(\widehat\theta-\theta)^2]/R_\Gamma\to1\), \(\widehat V/R_\Gamma\xrightarrow{\mathbb P_U}1\), \((\widehat\theta-\theta)/\sqrt{\widehat V}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\), and \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\mathbb P_U\{\theta\in[\widehat\theta\pm z_\alpha\sqrt{\widehat V}]\}\ge1-\alpha\)? Every within-unit cross-stage covariance term must be retained.
statements.justification: Exact oracle risk is not yet operational; feasible studentization is the genuine unresolved inference content.
statements.gap: BojinovRambachanShephard2021 uses assignment-path martingales, while ChenLi2025 randomizes adoption timing across clusters. Neither result covers independent unit hash scores reused through all stages of a nested threshold rollout with observed-panel learning of oracle weights.
statements.consumer: This would support design-based confidence intervals for cumulative effects in repeatedly measured hash-threshold rollout cohorts.

sampling_model.design: Known nested hash-threshold randomization given by the assignment construction \(Z\), with one independent uniform score per fixed unit and that score reused at every stage.
sampling_model.units: A fixed finite population \(I_n\) is repeatedly observed at every measured stage, and the complete unit-level panel \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is available; there is no superpopulation sampling randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: Irreversible own-unit exposure with \(0=p_0\le\cdots\le p_T=1\), carryover order \(L\), and the explicit convention \(p_s^{\mathrm{ext}}=0\) for \(s\le0\).
sampling_model.overlap: No positivity condition is needed for the linear target once \(X^{\mathsf T}w=c\); support sufficiency is characterized by the stage-frontier theorem.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The secular polynomial is removed by exact balance. In the regime \(n\to\infty\) with \(T\), \(r\), and \(L\) fixed, the oracle covariance depends on unobserved fixed lag coefficients; observed-panel covariance learning, oracle-risk equivalence, and feasible studentization are the open question.

estimand_functional: For a fixed horizon \(H\), precommitted endpoint schedule \(p\), and observed-wave set \(\mathcal S\), form the distinct interior-threshold blocks \(v_{t,q}\) and their span \(\mathcal V(p,\mathcal S)\) in Definition \(\mathrm{def:wave\text{-}threshold\text{-}block\text{-}span}\). Then \(\theta\) has an exactly design-unbiased observed-wave estimator if and only if \(\mathbf 1_{L+1}\in\mathcal V(p,\mathcal S)\). For any coefficients satisfying \(\sum_{t,q}\lambda_{t,q}v_{t,q}=\mathbf 1_{L+1}\), Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:fixed\text{-}schedule\text{-}wave\text{-}span\text{-}certificate}\) gives the explicit map \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{span}}=\sum_{t,q}\lambda_{t,q}\widehat\Delta_{t,q}\), where \(\widehat\Delta_{t,q}\) is the Horvitz--Thompson difference between the two adjacent positive-probability hash cells around \(q\), and gives its exact shared-score finite-population variance. The plateau \(L=3\), \(H=4\), \(p=(0,1/3,1/3,1,1)\), \(\mathcal S=\{2,4\}\) is feasible because its two blocks are \((1,1,0,0)^{\mathsf T}\) and \((0,0,1,1)^{\mathsf T}\). A single wave at \(t\) is the special case \(0<p^{\mathrm{ext}}_{t-L}\leq p_t<1\), with estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{one}}(t)\). At \(L\geq1\), \(H=L+1\), feasibility for some schedule requires and is implied by observing \(H\) and at least one \(s<H\); panel endpoint overlap is sufficient for the endpoint estimator on \(\{1,H\}\), but is not necessary for fixed-schedule identification. Under measurement at every threshold, \(T_{\min}^{\mathrm{panel}}(L)=\max\{2,L+1\}\). The restricted stage-mean benchmark remains \(\widehat\theta_w=w^{\mathsf T}M\), \(X(p)^{\mathsf T}w=c\), with oracle-risk benchmark \(w_\Gamma=\operatorname*{argmin}_{X(p)^{\mathsf T}v=c}v^{\mathsf T}\Gamma(p,b)v\).

The paper develops optimum regression designs for inference on one or several coefficients and gives polynomial-regression design calculations.
The paper shows, for symmetric Tchebycheff systems, that a design optimal for estimating a specified parameter is supported on one of two Tchebycheff point sets.

Theorem 3.1 gives sufficient optimality conditions for a \(T\)-period irreversible design maximizing the trace of the GLS precision matrix under the paper's specified lag model; its treated-fraction solution has five phases when the theorem's conditions hold.

tldr: The field-level kernel is a sharp support theorem for an irreversible hash-threshold rollout under novel maintained restrictions allowing unit-specific additive distributed-lag coefficients and unit-specific degree-\(r\) secular trends. The sustained direct-plus-carryover contrast is attainable with exactly \(T_{\min}(r,L)=\max\{r+2,L+1\}\) measured stages: a normalized binomial ramp and terminal finite-difference weights attain the bound, while explicit lag-deficit and trend-deficit aliases prove necessity. The row-space certificate is classical \(c\)-estimability specialized to this design, and the exact shared-hash covariance and singular quadratic program are supporting benchmarks rather than headline contributions. Feasible observed-panel covariance learning and studentization with \(n\to\infty\) and fixed \(T\), \(r\), and \(L\) remain the first-class open question.

project_justification.gap: Classical \(c\)-estimability and \(c\)-optimal regression design characterize whether and how a scalar linear parameter can be estimated and optimized over generic design spaces. Xiong, Athey, Bayati, and Imbens optimize \(T\)-period GLS trace precision for specified instantaneous and lagged effects, Cortez, Eichhorn, and Yu recover one polynomial rollout response by interpolation, and Aboukhamseen, Huda, and Bose optimize total-effect contrasts in two-period non-circular multi-treatment crossover designs with correlated errors. These results do not give a target-specific minimum-stage formula for one irreversible monotone hash-threshold path with degree-\(r\) calendar nuisance and arbitrary declared lag order, nor explicit target-active aliases at each support deficit.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a conditional schedule-sufficiency frontier for the cumulative direct-plus-carryover contrast. It must distinguish target estimability from full coefficient identification, certify the least feasible number and placement of measured stages, and exhibit a nonidentification direction whenever either the lag horizon or the polynomial nuisance exhausts the available support.
project_justification.fill: The project states the heterogeneous additive-lag and polynomial-trend equations as novel maintained restrictions, uses the classical row-space certificate only as supporting algebra, and makes the sole field-level theorem the sharp formula \(T_{\min}(r,L)=\max\{r+2,L+1\}\). A normalized binomial path and terminal finite differences attain the bound, while the zero lag-column alias and the interpolation-polynomial alias prove necessity. Exact shared-hash covariance and singular quadratic programming remain cited supporting context, and observed-panel covariance learning with oracle-risk equivalence and studentized coverage is the open inference rung.

related_work: Elfving1952, pp. 255--262, studies optimum allocation for estimating one linear combination of regression coefficients and supplies the geometric ancestor of \(c\)-optimality. KieferWolfowitz1959, pp. 271--294, develops computational optimum-design theory for inference on regression coefficients and includes polynomial-regression calculations. Studden1968, pp. 1435--1447, shows that for symmetric Tchebycheff systems a design optimal for a specified parameter is supported on one of two Tchebycheff point sets. These classical results explain the row-space and variance-minimization background, but their generic design spaces do not impose a single monotone endpoint path whose shifts simultaneously form \(L+1\) carryover columns; consequently they do not determine \(\max\{r+2,L+1\}\), prove its attainability by such a path, or construct the two deficit aliases. AboukhamseenHudaBose2021, pp. 253--261, obtains universally optimal designs for total-effect contrasts, the sum of direct and carryover effects, in two-period non-circular multi-treatment crossover experiments with correlated within-subject errors. That comparator allocates treatment sequences across repeatedly treated subjects; it does not study a single-treatment irreversible monotone hash-threshold rollout, degree-\(r\) calendar nuisance, arbitrary declared lag order, target-specific estimability, or a sharp minimum-stage support frontier. XiongAtheyBayatiImbens2023, Sections 3.1--3.3 and Theorem 3.1, studies a \(T\)-period irreversible experiment and gives sufficient optimality conditions for maximizing the trace of the infeasible-GLS precision matrix under a specified lag model. Its reported \(S\)-shape has five phases within the treated-fraction curve, not five measured periods; this proposal is informed by its shifted-lag design but does not attribute the heterogeneous unit-level lag or polynomial restrictions to that paper. CortezEichhornYu2022, Section 3, recovers a degree-bounded rollout mean curve from one more measurement than the degree bound by Lagrange interpolation; the new step is simultaneous annihilation of unit-specific calendar polynomials and equalization of shifted copies of one path. AtheyImbens2022 and RothSantAnna2023 provide supporting design-based variance and efficient-linear-estimation context rather than headline targets. BojinovRambachanShephard2021 derives finite-population limits from sequential assignment paths. ChenLi2025 studies cluster-level adoption-time randomization, whereas the present design uses independent unit hash scores reused across all threshold stages. HusseyHughes2007 and HughesHeagertyXiaRen2020 motivate separating exposure from calendar time but do not imply the maintained heterogeneous restrictions. LinkedInHash2020 documents deterministic hash assignment, and LinkedInTRex2020 documents successive allocation stages; these sources identify an operational consumer, not an implementation claim.
technical_internal_limitation: The minimum-stage theorem optimizes measured-stage count, not exact covariance risk among schedules with that count. The exact shared-hash covariance is the common-uniform kernel already covered by \(\texttt{exp\_rollout\_common\_uniform\_covariance\_design}\), specialized here to the lag notation, and minimization over exact-balance weights is standard singular quadratic-program machinery; neither is a headline contribution. The oracle weight \(w_\Gamma\) depends on fixed potential-outcome coefficients and is therefore only a benchmark. The unit-specific additive lag and exact polynomial-trend restrictions are maintained modeling conditions, so the certificate does not protect against treatment-history interactions, higher-order trend leakage, or misspecified carryover order.
honest_scope: The claims to be proved are the specialized row-space equivalence, the sharp support formula \(T_{\min}(r,L)=\max\{r+2,L+1\}\), the binomial-ramp witness, both support-deficit aliases, and the presolve identities. The support formula is the sole field-level kernel; generic \(c\)-estimability, the displayed shared-hash covariance expansion, and singular-KKT variance minimization are supporting context. The heterogeneous unit-level distributed-lag and polynomial-trend equations are novel maintained restrictions rather than consequences of the cited rollout, optimal-design, or stepped-wedge literature. Feasible observed-panel covariance estimation, oracle-risk equivalence, a primitive finite-population central limit theorem, and Wald coverage remain open as \(n\to\infty\) with \(T\), \(r\), and \(L\) fixed under the separately stated uniform fourth-moment, max-unit negligibility, and nondegenerate \(nR_\Gamma\) conditions. These three inference regularity conditions are not premises of identification or the support-frontier theorem. As a sanity boundary rather than a proof target, if \(a_{i,j}=\bar a_j\) and \(b_{i,\ell}=\beta_\ell\) for all units and indices, the same mean-design calculation applies. When \(L=0\), the frontier reduces to the \(r+2\) observations needed to difference a degree-\(r\) nuisance from one treatment contrast. When \(r=L=1\), it reduces to the verified three-stage schedule \(p=(0,1/6,1/2,1)\).
